stance_basis: described as conducting noise evaluation study and recommending attenuation measures, no position on project itself
summary: Bolt, Beranek and Newman, Inc. served as the noise evaluation consultant for the Randolph Urban Renewal project, conducting detailed computer-based noise level contour studies for areas adjacent to the proposed Downtown Expressway. The firm evaluated the effectiveness of various shielding barriers and recommended a combination of attenuation measures—including earth berms, fixed glazing, air-conditioning, and building orientation—to reduce noise exposure to HUD-acceptable levels. Their findings and recommendations were incorporated directly into the Randolph Project Plans.
complaint_summary: Bolt, Beranek and Newman evaluated the effect of incorporating a shielding barrier along Grayland Avenue on site noise levels, assessing barriers of 10, 15, and 20 feet in height and concluding that the 10-foot barrier would have a greatly reduced effect and should be eliminated from further consideration.
summary_quote: The Bolt Beranek and Newman report described on pages 18-22 of the Draft Statement evaluated the effectiveness of a number of shielding barriers of various heights.
